title: Trump ran on lowering prices. Now most Americans blame him for them.
text:

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump ran on lowering prices. Now most Americans blame him for them.

An October poll also found that most blame Trump's policies for making affordability struggles worse.

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump sits during an event on health care affordability in the Oval Office on April 23, 2026.Mark Schiefelbein/AP

Only 17 percent of Americans approve of how President Donald Trump is handling the cost of living, according to a recent poll from the Associated Press and NORC Center for Public Affairs Research.

This is a record low for both of Trump’s presidential terms—notable as he spent much of his 2024 campaign criticizing Democrats on the issue. About 70 percent, including about half of Republicans, said the president’s cost-of-living policies have been “worse than expected.”

The Associated Press reported that Trump’s economic approval mirrors Biden’s 28 percent in June 2022 during the initial years of the Covid-19 pandemic. A few months later, 55 percent of Americans said that affordability struggles were outside his control. Actual Article Body:
Voters overwhelmingly want to keep the Supreme Court bench capped at nine justices, a new poll found, despite Democrats’ push to pack the court.

A new McLaughlin Associates poll found that voters overwhelmingly support keeping the Supreme Court at nine justices and back the “Keep Nine Amendment.”

The amendment sought to require that the Supreme Court be comprised of nine justices. Notably, nearly every single House Republican and one Democrat, Don Davis of North Carolina, supported the amendment during a Sept. 2 vote that came to 212-206. Fifteen members did not vote. The measure failed to get the two-thirds majority needed to pass it.
